correctness.rationale: All definitions and quantifiers are explicit. With nonnegative b_i the denominator of the seasonal flow is at least one, giving global positivity; differentiation verifies the ODE formula. Diagonal fractional maps close under composition with exact coefficient updates, so the k-th iterate follows by induction. Three disjoint cases of the maximum positive multiplier give exact positive-winner limits, critical 1/k decay, or geometric extinction. The ratio identity and a strictly increasing scalar map exclude all nonfixed subharmonics, and direct differentiation yields every listed Floquet multiplier. Exact standard-library rational tests of the composition, iterates, timing witness, and neutral-simplex spectrum passed; the theorem is analytic, not extrapolated from tests.

originality.rationale: The discrete map itself is a known equal-row Leslie–Gower subclass and is not claimed as novel. The scoped contribution is the exact realization from arbitrary finite staggered multiplicative pulse schedules with periodic shared-crowding flow, the all-parameter closed-form iteration, strict pulse-timing independence of the competitive winner, complete critical and neutral-face classification, no subharmonics, and full Floquet spectrum. Sacker (2011) treats weak-coupling periodic Leslie–Gower coexistence, Hosack et al. (2025) local stability, Schreiber (2025) general impulsive invasion theory, and Courcelle et al. (2026) general pulse permanence. None of the accessible results implies the full scoped theorem. The original motivating preprint was not accessible in full, so historical-priority uncertainty remains.

value.rationale: The question of whether asynchronous pulse scheduling can change the winning population is motivated directly by periodic intervention models. The answer is a sharp, model-wide no under shared per-capita crowding even though the timing changes survivor density by a nonzero exact amount. The theorem completely classifies exclusion, critical polynomial extinction, neutral coexisting periodic-state simplices, local normal stability, and absence of subharmonics for all finite species counts and all admissible periodic coefficients. This establishes a transparent benchmark and a precise boundary of when scheduling alone can control species composition; it is not merely a parameter substitution or table recomputation. It does not purport to solve general competition dynamics.
